Within two hours the merchant replied that KORA40 is not their code, that the account advertising it is not theirs and has been reported, and that no sale was running.
At checkout the buyer accepted the Terms of Sale (version 2026-03), which say that placing an order means agreeing to the terms. Nothing in the store's policies mentions a 40% promotion.

This is a first-time customer with no earlier disputes. The claim looks like a misunderstanding caused by a third-party impersonation account, not bad faith. Still, the merchant isn't liable for a promotion it never offered.

risks: We have no records from the Instagram account, so we can't prove it isn't Kora Atelier's. The reviewer has to rely on the merchant's statement and the listing price.
If any official Kora Atelier channel ever posted a 40% code, the claim would succeed. The merchant should confirm that none did before filing.
Fighting may lose this first-time customer. A goodwill gesture outside the dispute, such as a small courtesy credit, is the merchant's call.

The checkout or discount system log showing that KORA40 has never existed as a code

brief.response_letter:
Kora Atelier charged the correct, advertised price for this order and never offered the 40% discount the buyer is claiming.

1. On 2026-10-14 the buyer ordered one Weekender in Cognac. The listed price is $284.00 and she was charged $284.00, with no other fees or charges (Exhibit A).

2. Two hours after ordering, the buyer emailed us. She said a code, KORA40, that she had seen on Instagram did not work at checkout, so she paid full price (Exhibit B). The checkout showed the full price before she paid.

Kora Atelier LLC, Brooklyn, NY. studio@koraatelier.example

brief.headline: Real duplicate payment we promised to refund and never did: accept and refund $68
brief.summary: Fatima Rahman paid for order KA-19335 through PayPal and then again by card three minutes later. On Oct 17 we confirmed both payments and promised to refund the PayPal one. No refund was ever issued, and she followed up on Oct 28. The card payment covers the wallet she received, so the $68 PayPal payment is a true duplicate. Accept the claim now, before a lost fight adds fees and costs us a customer.

reasoning.point: Our own account notes say the order was paid twice, through PayPal and then by card three minutes later.
The buyer reported the double charge on Oct 17. We replied that we could see both payments and would refund the PayPal one.
The order has no refunds on record, and on Oct 28 the buyer was still waiting for the refund we promised.
The wallet was delivered, but delivery does not answer a duplicate-payment claim. One delivery cannot justify two payments.
PayPal allows accept_claim with a REFUND here. Refunding now keeps a first-time customer and avoids chargeback fees on a case we cannot win.

risks: Before accepting, check the card processor to make sure the card payment was not refunded or charged back too. If it was, refunding the PayPal payment would mean giving the money back twice.
Once the claim is accepted, the $68 cannot be recovered.

Kora Atelier did not take a second payment for this item. The $142 PayPal charge is the only payment for the Market Tote in Tan, and the card payment the buyer mentions was for a different product.

1. On 2026-10-04 the buyer bought a Classic Belt in Cognac for $96 by card, in person at our Brooklyn Flea pop-up. That is the only card payment we have from her (Exhibit C).
2. The tan tote was sold out at the stall. On 2026-10-08 the buyer emailed us: "I'm ordering the tote online now, since you'd sold out of the tan one at the stall" (Exhibit B).
3. She placed online order KA-18984 the same day: one Market Tote in Tan, $142, paid through PayPal capture 5GX02276WH3318640. No card payment or other funding was used for this order (Exhibit A).
4. The tote shipped by USPS Ground Advantage, tracking 9400111899561237725519, and was delivered on 2026-10-12 to 245 Eastern Pkwy, Apt 5D, Brooklyn, NY 11238, the address on the transaction (Exhibit D).

The two payments were for two different products, $96 and $142, which matches her total spend of $238 with us. The tote was paid for once, through PayPal, and delivered. We ask that the dispute be decided in the seller's favor.
